title: Determinism at the Boundary: Where AI Belongs — Check

questions.prompt: Why is the AI search implemented as a deterministic mock rather than a live LLM call during development and testing?
questions.explanation: Determinism makes the endpoint testable: the same input yields the same output, which a live model cannot guarantee.
options: LLMs are too cheap to be worth using
A deterministic mock lets tests assert exact, repeatable results
Mocks are faster to type than real code
Netlify does not allow network calls

questions.prompt: Putting an LLM call directly inside `fieldSummary` would make identical requests potentially return different results, harming reproducibility.
questions.explanation: Model outputs vary across runs, so a recommendation derived from one in the core path would not be reproducible or easily auditable.

questions.prompt: What is the architectural principle behind keeping AI on a separate surface from the gateway?
questions.explanation: Isolating probabilistic AI from the deterministic core keeps the core testable and trustworthy and lets AI be swapped or disabled safely.
options: AI is always more accurate than deterministic code
Separate the correct-and-reproducible core from the helpful-but-probabilistic enhancement
All endpoints should use the same technology
The gateway cannot call any external service

questions.prompt: Why is an LLM's failure mode considered harder to handle than a service returning a 500?
questions.explanation: An explicit error is easy to detect and route around; a plausible-but-wrong answer can slip through unnoticed, which is more dangerous for decision-making.
options: An LLM can confidently return wrong data that looks valid
